sections.skill: Tell a model from the product built around it

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: What is a model in an AI system?

choices.text: The app's screen and buttons you tap
The company that sells the subscription
The trained part that turns input into output
The list of usage limits on an account

questions.correct_answer: The trained part that turns input into output
questions.intro: A MODEL is the trained part of an AI system: the learned patterns that turn input into output. A PRODUCT (an app, website or feature) wraps a model with other parts: a screen to type in, instructions the company adds, safety filters, tools such as web search, saved settings, and usage limits. The same model can sit inside several products that behave differently, and one product can switch models over time. So "this chatbot did X" does not mean every chatbot does X, and a product's feature, like saving files or browsing the web, may come from the product, not from the model itself.
questions.feedback: The model is the learned core; the product wraps it.

sections.skill: Compare an engine with the car around it

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: In the comparison, what is the AI model like?

choices.text: The steering wheel
The engine
The seats
The radio

questions.correct_answer: The engine
questions.intro: Think of a car ENGINE and the CAR built around it. The engine makes the power, but the car adds the steering wheel, seats, brakes, radio and speed limiter. The same engine can go into a sports car and a delivery van, and they will drive very differently. An AI MODEL is like the engine: it produces the output. The PRODUCT is like the car: it adds the screen, rules, tools and limits. If a van is slow, the reason might be its limiter, not its engine.
questions.feedback: The model produces the output, like an engine.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Check current product details instead of assuming

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: A blog post from two years ago says a product cannot read PDF files. You need to know today. What should you check?

choices.text: The product's current help pages or release notes
The same two-year-old blog post again
Nothing; products never change their features
A friend's experience with another product

questions.correct_answer: The product's current help pages or release notes
questions.intro: Because products change, details you learned about one can go out of date: a company may update its model, add or remove tools, or change limits without the name changing much. Different products may also use different kinds of models: a chatbot, a photo tagger and a translation feature are not interchangeable. When a result matters, check what the specific product says about itself today, such as its help pages, settings and release notes, rather than assuming from a friend's experience with a different product or from an old article.
questions.feedback: Check current, product-specific information.
